citation: Albanbay N, Tursynbek Y, Graffi K, Uskenbayeva R, Kalpeyeva Z, Abilkaiyr Z, Ayapov Y. Federated learning-based intrusion detection in IoT networks: performance evaluation and data scaling study. Journal of Sensor and Actuator Networks 14(4):78, 2025. doi:10.3390/jsan14040078

A1.evidence: Only 'computed globally on the aggregated test set after the final communication round'; no train/test split procedure stated.

A2.evidence: 'All models accept a 39-dimensional normalized input vector' (incl. CNN+BiLSTM); no windows.

A3.evidence: 'min-max scaling was applied to all features, mapping values to the [0, 1] range'; fit scope not stated.

A4.evidence: 'trained for 20 communication rounds' with '10 local epochs per round'.

A5.evidence: Centralized: 'conducted with the full dataset over 10 epochs' vs FL 20 rounds x 10 local epochs.

A6.evidence: 'Each model was additionally trained using a centralized approach' by the authors; no copied prior-work table.

A7.evidence: 'accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score' (plus macro variants, confusion matrices).

A8.evidence: 'Each client received a distinct combination of benign and malicious traffic, deliberately varying in attack types and their relative proportions.'

A9.evidence: No seeds, repeated runs, std or tests; each configuration 'treated as an independent experiment, initialized from scratch'.

notes: Baselines are the authors' centralized versions of the same DNN/CNN/CNN+BiLSTM models.
